definitions.explanation: A living organism too small to be seen with the naked eye, including bacteria, viruses, fungi, and protozoa. Used in scientific, medical, and food-production contexts.

examples.japanese: {微生物|びせいぶつ}を{顕微鏡|けんびきょう}で{観察|かんさつ}する。
examples.english: To observe microorganisms under a microscope.

examples.japanese: {土|つち}の{中|なか}には{多|おお}くの{微生物|びせいぶつ}が{生息|せいそく}している。
examples.english: Many microorganisms live in the soil.

examples.japanese: {発酵|はっこう}{食品|しょくひん}は{微生物|びせいぶつ}の{働|はたら}きを{利用|りよう}して{作|つく}られる。
examples.english: Fermented foods are made by utilizing the activity of microorganisms.

notes:
USAGE:
The word breaks down as {微|び} (minute) + {生物|せいぶつ} (living thing). Used in both scientific and everyday contexts. Japanese fermentation culture (sake, miso, soy sauce, natto) relies heavily on {微生物|びせいぶつ}, making this word common in food-related discussions as well as biology.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {微生物|びせいぶつ}{学|がく}: microbiology
- {微生物|びせいぶつ}の{繁殖|はんしょく}: proliferation of microorganisms
- {有害|ゆうがい}{微生物|びせいぶつ}: harmful microorganisms
- {腸内|ちょうない}{微生物|びせいぶつ}: gut microbes
